feedback: For a mis-ordered phagocytosis sequence, replay the engulf-then-digest order and ask which step must come before the pathogen can be broken down.
For a vaccination question answered as 'a cure', restate that vaccination happens before infection to prime memory cells, so it is protection in advance rather than a treatment during illness.
activities.intendedInsight: Learners consolidate the sequence of phagocytosis, the division of labour between white-blood-cell defences, and the vaccination and infection-vs-illness ideas.
learnerActions: Categorise example diseases as bacterial, viral or fungal.
Match each immune cell to its function (phagocyte→engulf and digest; lymphocyte→make specific antibodies; memory cell→faster, larger second response).
Put the stages of phagocytosis in order: approach → engulf → enclose → digest.
Answer short questions on how vaccination produces immunity and on the difference between infection and illness.
activities.title: Sequencing and categorising: checking the mechanism
